supplemental_reviewed_clauses.verbatim_extracted_text:
3.	 Regulatory  Reliance and Cooperation
•	
The regulatory environment is becoming increasingly complex and influenced by 
trade and globalization. Further, given the limitation of resources, governments 
cannot directly regulate all relevant aspects of medicines and health products 
across the life course of a product from pre-market to post-market phases. 
Hence, effective regulation cannot be achieved by individual countries acting 
on their own. Countries need to consider regulatory reliance and cooperation to 
ensure the safety and quality of medicines and health products.
•	
Efforts will be made to enhance the regulatory reliance and cooperation 
with international regulatory or reference authorities like the World Health 
Organization (WHO), European Medicines Agency (EMA), the U.S. Food and Drug 
Administration (FDA) for drug approvals etc. for:
-	
Improved efficiency by reducing duplication of efforts, allowing for faster 
access to medicines.
-	
Resource optimization and leveraging the expertise of larger, more 
established authorities. 
-	
Improved standards which promote the adoption of best practices and 
high standards.
-	
Public Health Protection to strengthen global responses to public 
health threats by aligning regulatory frameworks.
